decision: PROMISING, narrowly scoped to synthetic shared-plus-sparse-novel task stream
facts: PackNet-style independent sparse storage uses 1,536 per-task values and averages 9,358 B, with exact reconstruction.
Mirror shares a rank-3 128-coordinate basis, stores three codes per task, and splits private residuals only for four novel tasks; mean residual values 62.2 and serialized payload 1,658 B.
Mirror query NRMSE is 0.000394; no-split view NRMSE is 0.0996.
Generic robust shared-basis fit also splits four tasks, with 62.4 residual values, 1,959 B, and query NRMSE 0.000891.
Mirror total parameter values including shared basis/codes are approximately 482 versus 1,536 PackNet values (~69% fewer); payload is ~82% smaller.
Generic PCA baseline uses 2,626 B, ~178 residual values and query NRMSE 0.00398.
interpretation: Trying a View before per-task physical allocation can delay allocation on this constructed task stream. Mirror improves the storage-quality point over PackNet and modestly over the robust generic shared-basis control; however, the teacher was generated from the exact Mirror basis and codes are directly available, so the difference is not evidence of general learned Mirror advantage.
hypothesis: Supported as aligned synthetic allocation feasibility; general PackNet replacement and Mirror-specific learning advantage are not established.
counter_hypothesis: The shared tasks are generated exactly from the stored Mirror basis, giving it oracle coordinates; a better uncentered generic factorization or robust code fitting may close the remaining gap.
limitations: PackNet approximated as independent sparse task weights; no iterative pruning or training
Teacher shared tasks exactly use Mirror basis; latent codes directly supplied
No sequential optimizer retention, neural task quality, or inference latency
Generic robust control close but not byte-identical; uncentered robust factorization not tested
